title: Controllable Sim Agents with Behavior Latents (CNeVA)

control_signal.value: Per-agent behavior latent over K=4 reward channels (safety, map, speed, accel), set as one-hot or partial steering vector with a channel mask and guidance weight.

control_mechanism.value: Latent inferred in closed form from per-channel discounted returns; it enters the flow generator as an extra cross-attention token, with classifier-free guidance trained under mixed channel masks.

base_model.value: Conditional flow-matching (rectified-flow) trajectory generator, Transformer decoder with 6 layers, 8 heads, width 512; Euler sampler with 10 steps.

datasets.value: Waymo Open Motion Dataset under the WOSAC protocol (1.1 s history, 8 s rollout, up to 128 agents).

metrics.value: WOSAC realism meta-metric and minADE; controllability via channel steering matrix (CSM) diagonals and trajectory divergence; guardrails: stall fraction, retained speed.

controllability_evidence.value: Table 2 CSM diagonals at w=1.5: safety +0.66, map +0.61, speed +8.15, accel +8.76; unconditional: +0.06, +0.06, -3.33, +4.77. Test realism 0.7145, minADE 1.80 m.

stated_limitations.value: Map controllability depends on the reward definition (physical off-road and lane-centerline measures fail to steer); guardrails degrade at larger steering magnitude, so results use calibrated rho=1.

notes: Table 2 flattened in packet; the unconditional column values are read from the order given. Realism is mid-leaderboard, below non-controllable imitation models.
